title: Service profiling experiment matrix and SLO extrapolation playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes a standardized experiment matrix, data schema, measurement methodology, and extrapolation techniques for predicting service-level objective (SLO) behavior at scale. It is intended to help engineering teams validate capacity changes, quantify expected P50/P95/P99 latency shifts when scaling QPS or changing kernel/quantization profiles, and produce evidence for release decisions.

Goals and non-goals
-------------------
- Goals:
  - Provide a repeatable set of profiling experiments for inference services (inference-proxy, runtime-batcher, variant-router).
  - Define minimum data quality and sample sizes for reliable quantile estimates.
  - Offer an extrapolation method to estimate SLOs at higher QPS and alternate batch/sequence distributions.
  - Produce a clear runbook for diagnosing and mitigating regressions discovered by experiments.
- Non-goals:
  - This is not a full capacity planner for fleet-level autoscaling (see eng-sre capacity-planning).
  - It does not replace real production chaos testing; it's a controlled profiling toolset.

Scope and applicable services
----------------------------
This playbook applies to services that are on the inference request path:
- inference-proxy (edge -> ingress point, request enrichment)
- runtime-batcher (continuous batching layer that aggregates requests to model shards)
- model-executor (per-GPU inference process; capture as aggregate metrics where direct instrumentation is unavailable)

Key SLOs targeted
----------------
- Request latency (P50, P95, P99) measured at the API boundary (inference-proxy) with tokenized request/response timestamps.
- Token throughput (tokens/sec) and model-level throughput (inferences/sec) as secondary metrics.
- Error rate (5xx) and circuit-breaker invocations.

Experiment matrix (canonical)
----------------------------
Run experiments across a Cartesian product of the following dimensions. Each cell is a single experiment run (30–60 minutes steady state recommended).
1) QPS target: [10, 50, 200, 500, 1000]
2) Sequence length buckets: [short (<=64), mid (65-512), long (>512)]
3) Batch size behavior: [no-batching, observed-batching, forced-batch=16, forced-batch=32]
4) Model runtime profile: [fp32, int8-quant, kernel-optimized]
5) Hardware class: [A100, H100, T4] (if available)
6) KV/prefix cache hit-rate: [0%, 50%, 90%]

Minimum experiment duration and sample sizes
-----------------------------------------
- Warmup: 5 minutes to allow KV caches and batchers to stabilize.
- Steady-state collection: 30 minutes per cell.
- Minimum successful requests per cell: 50,000 or 30 minutes whichever yields more samples.
- For quantile stability, target at least 1,000 samples in the P99 tail bucket.

Data schema and required telemetry
--------------------------------
Collect both aggregated time-series and per-request traces/samples. Required fields for per-request samples (CSV/JSON):
- timestamp_utc
- request_id
- service (inference-proxy | runtime-batcher | model-executor)
- request_qps_target
- sequence_length_tokens
- batch_size
- kernel_profile (string)
- hardware_type
- kv_cache_hit (true|false)
- latency_ms_total
- latency_ms_ingress
- latency_ms_batching
- latency_ms_inference
- success (true|false)
- error_code (if any)
- sample_tags (comma-separated labels)

Example CLI commands
--------------------
- Start a canonical profile collection (example):
  rinfer profile collect --service inference-proxy --duration 45m --qps 200 --seq-dist mid --batch-policy observed --out /tmp/profiles/ip-qps200-mid.json
- Convert profile to aggregated metrics:
  rinfer profile summarize --input /tmp/profiles/ip-qps200-mid.json --out /tmp/summary/ip-qps200-mid.summary.json

Extrapolation methodology
-------------------------
We provide a pragmatic, defensible extrapolation approach rather than a single black-box model. Two levels of extrapolation are supported:
A) Dimension-preserving interpolation/extrapolation (statistical):
  - For each metric (P50/P95/P99), fit a smooth monotonic function over QPS (use log(QPS) as independent variable).
  - Use quantile regression (e.g., linear quantile regression on log-QPS) to estimate the quantile at an unseen QPS.
  - Provide bootstrap confidence intervals (95%) using sampled experiment runs.
B) Queueing-informed extrapolation (system-aware):
  - Model runtime-batcher as M/G/1 queue with service time distribution derived from sampled latency_ms_inference.
  - For each QPS target, compute expected queueing delay and add to measured inference latency to estimate end-to-end latency.
  - Apply correction factor for batching nonlinearities observed in profiling (empirically derived multiplier).

Operational pseudocode (high-level)
-----------------------------------
```
# inputs: list of experiment summaries M = [{qps, p50, p95, p99, service_profile}]
# step 1: fit quantile_regression models on log(qps) -> quantile
models = fit_quantile_regression(M, quantiles=[0.5,0.95,0.99])
# step 2: if queueing extrapolation requested:
service_time_dist = estimate_service_time_distribution(latency_samples)
queue_delay(qps) = mg1_expected_wait(service_time_dist, qps)
predicted_p95 = models['p95'](log(qps)) + queue_delay(qps) * correction_factor
# output: predicted quantiles + 95% bootstrap CI
```

Quality gates and acceptance criteria
------------------------------------
- Calibration check: when extrapolating to a QPS for which an experiment exists, predicted P95 must be within ±12% of measured P95 for the same cell. If not, rerun experiments and review data collection fidelity.
- Minimum CI width: if 95% bootstrap CI for P95 is wider than ±25% relative, mark the cell as low-confidence and increase sample duration or repeat runs.
- Regression triage: any predicted increase in P95 > 20% compared to baseline must open a triage ticket (label: perf-regression) and follow the runbook below.

Regression runbook (for predicted or observed regressions)
--------------------------------------------------------
1) Verify instrumentation and data integrity: check timestamps, clock skew, and sampling consistency across services.
2) Reproduce minimal failing experiment: isolate single dimension (e.g., keep QPS and seq-length constant) and run targeted 15m test.
3) Compare span-level breakdown: ingress vs batching vs inference.
4) If batching contribution > 40% of delta: inspect runtime-batcher logs for scheduling delays and nonideal batch composition.
5) If inference contribution dominant: capture model-executor telemetry and check kernel selection, quantization toggles, GPU utilization, and memory pressure.
6) Temporary mitigations: reduce max batch size, enable forced prefix caching, degrade to lower model variant, or redirect traffic to dedicated capacity pool.
7) Permanent fixes: raise follow-up engineering story with root cause and rollout plan.

Owner and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Experiment design and execution: Performance Platform (perf-platform) team (primary).
- Data ingestion and summary tooling: Observability Platform team (metrics and traces).
- Runtime-level changes (batcher/kernel): Eng Serving Runtime (owners: runtime-batcher, kernel-and-scheduling).
- Decision to change customer-facing SLOs: Product and SRE leadership.

Templates and artifacts to attach
--------------------------------
- experiment-matrix.csv (columns: qps, seq_bucket, batch_policy, kernel, hw, cache_hit_rate, run_id)
- sample-schema.json (per-request sample definition)
- example-summary.json (expected aggregator output)
- artifact naming convention: svc-experiment-<service>-<qps>-<seq>-<batch>-<kernel>-<hw>-<timestamp>.json

Example aggregated table (one line per experiment)
-------------------------------------------------
| run_id | qps | seq_bucket | batch_policy | kernel | hw | p50_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | err_rate | comments |
| r-20260203-01 | 200 | mid | observed | int8 | H100 | 34 | 112 | 240 | 0.02% | steady-state 40m |

Testing checklist before release
-------------------------------
- All target cells in experiment matrix executed at least once.
- Calibration checks passed for holdout QPS points.
- Extrapolation notebook and bootstrap artifacts attached to the run ticket.
- Runbook and mitigation steps documented on the ticket.

References and related docs
---------------------------
- Eng Serving Runtime: sequence-length-aware-kernel-selection-guidelines-2026
- Performance: predictable-cost-latency-simulator-specification-2026
- Observability: telemetry-ingestion-and-retention-guidelines-2025

Appendix A — Quick checklist for engineers
-----------------------------------------
1) Pick canonical experiment cell and run warmup + 30m steady window.
2) Ensure rinfer profile collect uses the --trace-sample-rate 0.01 for per-request traces.
3) Upload artifact to perf-bucket with metadata tag run-owner.<owner> and link in ticket.
4) Run extrapolation script and attach results: scripts/extrapolate_qps.py --input /tmp/summaries/*.json --target-qps 1000 --out /tmp/predictions.json
